faq_slots.question: Why does water come through the ceiling under the shower?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Use the assigned symptom's meaning and its linked local issue. Three genuinely different routes in plain words: a seal round the tray or the bath that has let go, a waste joint under the floor, grout or a tray that flexes letting water behind the tiles. Say that the water runs along the boards and the joists before it shows, so the damp patch and the leak are seldom in the same place, and that a new bead of silicone over the old one is not the fix where the floor is already wet. Then what the local housing adds (an upstairs bathroom over a kitchen, a flat over a neighbour), then what the fitter looks at. Never a step the customer could try on electrics near the leak.

faq_slots.question: Can the toilet, the sink or the shower move to a different wall?
faq_slots.answer_brief: What decides it, from the trade facts stages and rule rows, in plain words: a waste pipe has to run downhill to the drain, so a basin or a shower moves more easily than a toilet, which usually stays close to the soil pipe; moved further, a toilet usually needs a new soil connection or a pumped unit, and a pumped unit usually depends on there being another toilet in the home that drains by gravity. New or altered drainage can bring building control in. 'Usually' throughout; never a document's name; no figure.

faq_slots.question: Who does the gas and electrical work in a new kitchen or bathroom?
faq_slots.answer_brief: The rule of the trade from the trade facts Table C and E rows, never a boast. Gas first: a hob, a cooker or a boiler is connected or moved by an engineer on the Gas Safe Register, registered for that kind of work. Then the electrics: a new circuit, a new fuse board, and wiring in or close to a bath or shower are the jobs that need a sign off. A registered electrician certifies that work themselves; otherwise building control has to be told and inspects it. A like for like swap elsewhere in the house usually needs no notice, though it is still tested. The customer keeps the paperwork. This business's own registrations only from [CV: verified_logos] and the accreditation client values; when none is on file, the rule alone and nothing about who this business uses. Never a step the customer could try.

faq_slots.question: Will my new kitchen or bathroom need planning permission or building control?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Point at the trade facts rule rows (Table C) and write what usually applies, with "usually" or "in most cases", keeping the two approvals apart: an ordinary refit inside the house usually needs no planning permission; a listed home usually needs consent even for work inside; a conservation area on its own does not change an internal refit. Building control is a different question and comes in where the job moves or adds drainage, puts a bathroom or a toilet where there was none, alters the structure, or includes electrical work that has to be certified; a registered installer can certify some of that work themselves, otherwise an application is made. Gas work is done by an engineer on the Gas Safe Register. What the customer does about it only as the row gives it; what this business arranges only from [CV: handles_planning]. No figure; never an Act's, a document's or a part's name.

cards.title: A room laid out for someone else
cards.brief: A situation card, not a fault: in a kitchen, nowhere beside the hob to set a pan down, a fridge door that swings across the only way through, a table nobody can get round, one person cooking while the rest stand in the doorway; in a bathroom, a queue at breakfast for the one bathroom in the house, a bath nobody uses on the wall a shower could have, no toilet downstairs. The one cause this card makes: a layout set for a different household. What decides it is the layout, not the size: where the sink, the hob and the fridge sit and the worktop between them; in a bathroom, where the soil pipe and the waste run, which fixes how far the toilet can move (the trade facts design and survey stages). What the work gives them, in plain words: the room planned round how they use it (worktop either side of the hob, a straight run reshaped into an L, a bath swapped for a walk in shower, an en suite or a cloakroom where the drainage allows it). By category: Kitchen Renovator reads it in the kitchen; Bathroom Renovator as the bathroom, the en suite or the cloakroom; Remodeller and Construction Company as whichever room the client's services cover. Never a lifestyle pitch, never a fault invented for it, never a judgement on the room they have now.
cards.mechanism: a layout set for a different household

cards.title: Water showing up where it should not
cards.brief: Problem led, from the trade facts signs rows: in a kitchen, a worktop joint that has lifted or an edge by the sink gone swollen, the cupboard under the sink soft at the base; in a bathroom, silicone gone black and lifting, cracked grout, water on the floor outside the shower, a damp patch on the ceiling of the room below. The one cause this card makes: a seal or a joint at the surface that has let water through, so the board, the floor or the ceiling behind it is wetter than it looks. Say the route the water takes in plain words (along the top of the board and into its cut edge, down behind the tiles, along the floorboards and the joists before it shows) and that the fix starts with finding where it gets in, never with a new bead of silicone run over the old one; what putting it right usually involves from the done badly rows (a sink cut out sealed, a tray bedded solid, a joint remade). What the business does only from confirmed practices. Never alarming, never a promise that the leak is small. Not the tanking behind the tiles: the service pages own that.
cards.mechanism: a seal or a joint at the surface that has let water through

cards.title: Things that move when they should not
cards.brief: Problem led: doors that rub and gaps that widen, a worktop joint that has opened, a shower tray that gives underfoot, tiles that sound hollow, a basin or a rail that shifts when leant on. The one cause this card makes: whatever it was fixed to was never made solid and level (units not levelled before the worktop went on, a tray on nothing solid, tiles on a wall that flexes, a rail into plasterboard with nothing behind it), so every use works the joint or the fixing loose (the trade facts done badly rows). Say what the fix usually involves in plain words from the stages: units set level and fixed to the wall before a worktop is templated, a tray on a solid and level bed before anything is tiled, timber or board fixed inside the wall before it is tiled wherever anything heavy hangs or is held. By category: Kitchen Renovator reads it in the units and the worktop; Bathroom Renovator in the tray, the tiles, a wall hung basin or toilet and the rails. No figure (no tile weight, no board thickness), never a dig at another trade.
cards.mechanism: fixed to something that was never made solid and level

cards.title: A room that has become hard to use
cards.brief: A situation and the pack's need led split in one: a bath side that has become a climb, a shower with a step up onto the tray, nothing solid to hold, a toilet too low or too far from a wall; in a kitchen, an oven at floor level, cupboards out of reach, a corner nobody can get into. The one cause this card makes: the room asking more of the person than it used to (the step, the reach, the grip, the room to turn). What decides the answer is the room and its drainage, from the trade facts stages: a shower with no step needs the floor formed with a fall to the drain and waterproofed as a wet room floor; a rail needs a fixing into something solid behind the tiles; a toilet raised or moved within reach of the soil pipe; an oven raised, drawers in place of low cupboards, a worktop at a height that suits. What the work gives them is written as what the person will be able to do (shower standing or seated, get in without a step, hold something that takes their weight, reach what they use), never their age, their diagnosis or their condition. A council grant towards adaptations only as something that may be available after the council's own assessment and can be means tested, never promised, no figure. By category: Bathroom Renovator reads it in the bathroom; Kitchen Renovator as reach and working height. Never clinical, never pitying.

faq_slots.answer_brief: From the trade facts rule rows for this service only, put as what usually applies, with "usually" or "in most cases", and the approvals kept apart. What the customer does only as the row gives it; what this business arranges only from [CV: handles_planning]. Never a figure, a document's name or a part letter; never a step the customer could try. Where the rows give no rule, say no permission is usually needed for this work at a home and leave it there.

faq_slots.question: What does your [SERVICE_LOWER] service include?
faq_slots.answer_brief: The What's Included items said as a sentence, in other words: the measuring, the strip out, first fix, the waterproofing or the units, the finishes, the tests. Supply and fit or fit only from the client values. What it does not cover (the gas connection, the certified electrics where this business holds no registration) only from the services list and [CV: verified_logos], with one sibling service page or the category page linked. Never 'on this page' or 'listed above': name the work.

faq_symptom.frame: [SYMPTOM]: why does it happen, and what can be done?
faq_symptom.answer_brief: The symptom and its linked local issue, answered as asked. Say where the water or the fault comes from in plain words and the route it takes before it shows, then what the local housing or water adds (hard water on screens and valves, an upstairs bathroom over the kitchen, a flat's shared stack, the layout an era built with), then what this service does about it. One figure at most. Never a step the customer could try on gas or electrics; never a bead of silicone as the fix for a wet floor.

cards.title: The room that gets in the way of the day
cards.brief: The customer's situation: cooking with nowhere to set a pan down, a fridge door that swings across the only way through, washing dried on the radiators because there is nowhere for a machine, a queue for the one bathroom at breakfast, a guest sent upstairs because there is no toilet down, a television on a stand with its cables across the floor, an alcove no cupboard fits. What decides it: the layout and what the room already has to give (where the water, the waste and the soil pipe run and how far they can move, the length of worktop between the sink and the hob, an alcove or the space under the stairs with the depth for a toilet or a run of shelves, a wall that will carry the weight and the wiring of a media wall), from the trade facts survey and design stages for this service. What the work gives them: the room planned round the way they use it, named from the stages for this service. Never a fault invented for it, never a lifestyle pitch, never a judgement on the room they have.
cards.mechanism: a layout that does not fit how the household uses the room

cards.title: Which way to do it
cards.brief: The customer's situation: they are weighing two or three ways of doing it (a bath against a walk in shower, tiles against panels, laminate against stone, rigid against flat pack units, new doors against new units, an en suite shower against a cloakroom with a basin, electric against water fed heating under a new floor, a recessed against a surface mounted media wall). What decides it: the room (where the drains fall, what the floor is made of, the water pressure and the hot water system a shower will run on, what the wall is made of where anything heavy hangs), how the household uses it and how much looking after they want, from the trade facts materials and methods cell for this service. What the work gives them: the option that suits their room, never the one that is best in general. A named product only from [CV: materials_methods]; never a brand. No claim about cost, lifespan or value unless the rows or the client values give it.
cards.mechanism: the room's services and its use deciding the option

cards.title: The part you will never see again
cards.brief: The customer's situation: they have a cheaper quote, or a plan to do it themselves, and want to know what the difference buys. What decides it: the layer hidden once the room is finished (units set level and fixed to the wall before the worktop is templated, the tanking behind the tiles and round every joint and pipe, the tray or the former on a solid and level bed with its fall to the drain, wastes with enough fall and a trap that keeps its seal, timber or board in the wall for anything that hangs or is held, the extractor ducted outside, a new circuit certified and a hob connected by an engineer on the Gas Safe Register), which is where a quick job cuts corners and shows a year or two later as a swollen edge, a black bead or a damp patch on the ceiling below (the trade facts done badly rows). What the work gives them: that layer done as the stages name it, with the certificates for the parts that need them. One specific from the stages for this service; no figure, no standard's number; never a dig at another trade.
cards.mechanism: the layer behind the finish deciding how long it lasts

cards.title: Living without the room while it is done
cards.brief: The customer's situation: they want to know how long they will be without a kitchen or a bathroom and what happens in which order. What decides it: the order of work from the trade facts stages for this service (the strip out; first fix plumbing and electrics; plastering and its drying; units, or the waterproofing and the tiling; a worktop templated only once the units are fixed and made away from the house; second fix; the tests and the sign offs; the cure of tanking, adhesive, grout or a coating before the room is used). What the work gives them: an honest picture of which stages take the room out of use, which wait on something made elsewhere, and what can be kept running. What this business does about it (a temporary sink, the other bathroom kept usable, the washing machine reconnected each night, the same team start to finish) only from confirmed practices (same_team_throughout, stage_updates, tidy_each_day). Never a duration, a date or a day by day plan: the trade facts give none; never a claim to manage every trade unless the client values give it.
cards.mechanism: the order of work deciding how long the room is out of use

cards.title: Kitchens and bathrooms where the house put them
cards.brief: The town profile's housing era and what it was built with: a terrace with the kitchen in a narrow wing at the back, so the units run along one wall; a semi built with the toilet and the bathroom as two small rooms upstairs, often knocked into one; a post war house with a small kitchen and a larder beside it; a new build with stud walls and a compact en suite. The one cause this card makes: the houses built with the kitchen and the bathroom where their decade put them. Say what that means for the work (a long single run, a wall taken down between two small rooms, a soil pipe on the outside wall deciding where the toilet can go), from the profile only; where it gives no era, the general point and nothing about this town's houses. Never the state of anyone's room today, never that the kitchens or bathrooms here are dated.
cards.mechanism: the houses built with the kitchen and the bathroom where their decade put them

cards.title: Limescale on everything the water touches
cards.brief: Screens that fog within weeks, taps crusted at the spout, a shower that loses its flow. Say first that scale in a hard water area is the water, not a fault. The one cause this card makes: the hardness of the town's water, from the profile or the water company's published data only, never invented. What it changes in the work: the shower valve and the screen chosen for it, the sealant round the screen, a softener only where the client's services list has one and never by brand. Where the research gives no hardness, say nothing about the water and read the card instead as the steam of a bathroom with no outside wall or a small window, and the extractor it needs ducted outside. Never a health claim, never a promise the scale will not return.
cards.mechanism: the hardness of the town's water

cards.title: Flats, stairs and the shared stack
cards.brief: A toilet that cannot move far, a leak that shows in the flat below, units carried up three flights, nowhere to park a van or sit a skip. The one cause this card makes: the shared soil stack and the shared floors of a flat. What it means for the work: the layout kept close to the stack, the floor treated as the neighbour's ceiling (the waterproofing and the water tests done before the floor is closed), the freeholder or the lease usually having to agree before a bathroom moves ('usually', never an Act's name), deliveries and waste planned round the stairs. From the profile where it gives the flats; otherwise read as the house's own upstairs bathroom and the room beneath it. Never a judgement on the flats.
cards.mechanism: a bathroom or a kitchen tied to a soil stack shared with the flats above and below

cards.title: Older homes and what the strip out meets
cards.brief: A listed home where even work inside usually needs consent (the trade facts rule rows), an older house where materials are checked before anything is cut into (no year), walls out of plumb and floors out of level under the old units. The one cause this card makes: what an older house was built with, met once the room is out. Say it as what the work meets and allows for, never as a claim about what is behind the walls of any street (no pipework, no wiring claimed in advance: the pack's section 3): 'often' and 'can', never 'will'. What the business does about it (a survey before suspect material is disturbed, levelling and packing, making good in the quote) only from confirmed practices and the stages. Never a judgement on the houses.
cards.mechanism: what an older house was built with, met once the room is out

cost.h2: What Affects the Cost of [WORK] in [TOWN]

cards.title: Carrying it up and getting it in
cards.brief: Terraced streets with no parking outside, flats with stairs and no lift, a kitchen at the back reached through the house: units, a bath and a stone worktop carried by hand, deliveries timed to the street. Say why that adds time, from the profile where it gives the housing. No figure.

cards.title: Moving the room away from the stack
cards.brief: In a flat, or an older house with the soil pipe on the back wall, moving the toilet means a new connection or a pumped unit with its own conditions; a layout that keeps it near costs less. 'Usually'; never a document's name. No figure.

cards.title: Listed homes and the lease
cards.brief: Consent before work inside a listed home, a lease that usually has to agree before a bathroom moves: the paperwork adds time and some things are not allowed. From the dossier rules only; never the law's name. No figure.

cards.title: What the old room was built on
cards.brief: Floors out of level, walls that need plastering before units go on, an old leak under the floor, older materials checked before they are disturbed (no year): what has to be put right before anything new goes in. Said as what the work meets, never as a judgement on the homes. No figure.

faq_slots.answer_brief: From [CV: quote_method] and the confirmed practices only: what the customer sends, what the business looks at in the room (the measurements, where the services run, the floor and the walls, how things get in), what comes back. No timescale unless [CV: response_time] is set.

The order of work as the reason (the strip out, first fix, plastering and its drying, units or the waterproofing and tiling, a worktop templated once the units are in, second fix, the tests and sign offs, the cure before the room is used), and where the town profile gives the housing (flats and their stairs, a terrace reached through the house, a listed home and its consent) what it does to that order.
